table_title: For each of five major scientific disciplines (Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Mathematics, Astronomy), list five notable foundational scientists from each discipline with their nationality, approximate era, and most important contribution.
db_analog: SELECT discipline, list_position, scientist, nationality, era, contribution FROM scientists WHERE discipline IN ('Physics','Chemistry','Biology','Mathematics','Astronomy') ORDER BY discipline, list_position
temporal_note: Wikipedia per-scientist articles accessed 2026-04-29. Universe of 5 disciplines (Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Mathematics, Astronomy) is anchored to Wikipedia 'Branches of science' which classifies all 5 as major disciplines (Physics/Chemistry/Astronomy under Natural-Sciences/Physical-Science; Biology under Natural-Sciences/Life-Science; Mathematics under Formal-Sciences). Per-discipline 5-scientist selections are curator-chosen notable foundational figures from each discipline (cycle-2 audit retitled cycle-0's 'widely-cited' to 'notable foundational' because 'widely-cited' implied citation/ranking evidence the staged sources do not provide) and corroborated row-by-row against the scientist's Wikipedia article for nationality, era, and one-sentence contribution. Schema follows the cycles 1+2+3 lessons from prior scaled_enumeration instances (world_religions_top5_holy_sites, twentieth_century_decade_inventions): selection-not-ranked framing in table_title; composite PK (Discipline, Scientist) with List Position as a non-key numeric display ordinal; per-row Wikipedia article cited from cycle 0 to avoid the audit-driven citation expansion that those prior instances incurred. All 25 scientists with end-of-life dates died before 2025 (cycle-1 audit fix: replaced James Watson 1928-2025 with Francis Crick 1916-2004 to keep the Era column cutoff-stable for pre-2025 LLMs while preserving the DNA-double-helix attribution; Crick is the universally co-credited co-author of the 1953 Nature paper). The 'Era' column uses year-year format for most rows ('1643-1727'); Euclid uses 'fl. 300 BC' (flourished, conventional dating) because precise dates are unknown for ancient figures. The 5-per-discipline row universe is curator-chosen notable foundational figures from each discipline's Wikipedia 'List of [Xists]' membership universe (cycle-1 audit fix: added per-discipline list articles as discipline-membership universe anchors so the row universe is now source-defined-membership + curator-display selection rather than purely curator selection).
_extraction_notes: Universe: 5 disciplines (Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Mathematics, Astronomy) anchored to Wikipedia 'Branches of science' which classifies all 5 as major disciplines. Discipline-membership universe (which scientists count as physicists / chemists / etc.) anchored to each discipline's Wikipedia 'List of [Xists]' article (cycle-1 audit fix; cycle-0 had only the universe anchor + per-scientist articles, leaving the row-universe definition unsupported). Per-discipline 5-scientist selection: curator-chosen notable foundational figures from each discipline's source-defined membership; each row's Nationality / Era / Contribution values are individually cited to that scientist's Wikipedia article. Watson (1928-2025) was replaced with Francis Crick (1916-2004) at cycle-1 to keep the Era column cutoff-stable for pre-2025 LLMs while preserving the DNA-double-helix biology pick. source_urls[0] is the discipline-universe anchor; source_urls[26-30] are the discipline-membership universe anchors; source_urls[1-25] are per-scientist value-source articles. Schema applies the cycles 1+2+3 lessons from world_religions_top5_holy_sites and twentieth_century_decade_inventions: (a) table_title says 'list five notable foundational scientists' (selection framing; cycle-0 'widely-cited' retitled at cycle-2 to drop the citation/ranking implication) rather than 'list the 5 most influential scientists' (ranked framing) because Wikipedia does not enumerate definitive ranked top-5 lists per discipline; (b) composite PK is (Discipline, Scientist) with List Position as a non-key numeric column. Selection rationale per discipline is documented in decision_log. No row duplications across disciplines: Newton appears only in Physics (not Mathematics), Galileo only in Astronomy (not Physics), even though both contributed to multiple disciplines. Within-discipline order is chronological (earliest birth year first). Result: 5 disciplines x 5 scientists = 25 rows x 6 columns, composite PK on (Discipline, Scientist), 0 duplicate PKs. Nationality column ranges over 12 distinct values (English, Scottish, German-born, Danish, French, Russian, Polish-French, American, Swedish, Austrian, Italian, German-British, Polish, Ancient Greek, Swiss, German). Some Wikipedia articles describe scientists with hybrid nationalities (Einstein 'German-born' later Swiss/American; Curie 'Polish and naturalised-French'; Herschel 'German-British'; Copernicus born in Royal Prussia, part of Poland) — the staged values use the article's primary phrasing; document in normalization_decisions.
